llm_input:
Synopsis:
Player interacted with the knocked out hag after combat with her. Player can cut Vanra out of the hag and save her.

Cluster Contexts:
- LOW_BlushingMermaid_SavingVanra.json: The player has just fought and knocked Auntie Ethel unconscious after she shed a human disguise and revealed herself as a hag. Ethel had bragged that she swallowed Lora’s missing child, Vanra, and is now physically distended with the child inside. In this scene the immediate option is to cut Ethel open to try to free and save Vanra; companions who confronted Ethel earlier may be present and react. Earlier choices (whether you killed or spared Lora, or how you dealt with Ethel’s bargains and taunts) affect tone and companions’ responses but not the basic fact that Vanra is inside the hag.
- LOW_BlushingMermaid_VanraSaved.json: The dialogue with saved Vanra, she was either vomitted out or carved from the hag by players.
- LOW_BlushingMermaid_PAD_HagCombatStart.json: PAD for when hag combat starts.Top one - should hint players that killing the hag will kill the child she ate.Bottom one - players know how to kill the hag/get vanra out. I chose the kill one for the generic, but feel free for your origins to focus on saving varna.
- LOW_BlushingMermaid_VomitsOutVanra_Hag.json: If Marrow of Mercy is thrown in the burning Circle of Pearls while Vanra is still alive inside the hag, the hag will vomit her out in this dialogue
- LOW_BlushingMermaid_DisguisedHag.json: The player has already found Vanra and returned her to her mother Lora at the Blushing Mermaid; Lora is distraught and Vanra is traumatized and largely catatonic. The woman posing as Captain Grisly at the inn is actually a hag (Auntie Ethel) in disguise — the real Captain Grisly has been locked away with a hag mask on and might be rescued later. In this scene the hag accuses Lora of making up the kidnapping, inflames the situation, and attempts to manipulate the player into murdering Lora by offering gold. If you refuse, the hag immediately drops the disguise and reveals her true form; if you agree and kill Lora she is delighted and transforms — companions may be present during these choices.

Dialogue Excerpts (up to 3 samples, ordered):
Sample 1:
- Narrator: *Auntie Ethel lies unconscious - her stomach bulging from the child she ate.* (node 3)
- Player: Cut Vanra out. (node 1)

context: You have just fought and knocked Auntie Ethel unconscious; she has shed a human disguise and lies bloated because she bragged she swallowed Lora’s missing child, Vanra. The immediate option in this scene is to cut the hag open to try to free and save Vanra — other scripted means (forcing the hag to vomit, using specific items, or carving the child out) can also result in Vanra being recovered. Companions who confronted Ethel earlier may be present and will react, and earlier choices (whether you spared or killed Lora, or how you handled Ethel’s bargains and taunts) change tone and responses but do not alter the fact that Vanra is inside. Note there is risk tied to the hag’s death: killing or destroying her during combat can endanger the child, so extracting Vanra alive requires careful action.
